items.t: SpaceX and Google both said no. Now his software is riding a SpaceX rocket next to Google’s
items.d: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.
items.fullText: The way Rama Afullo tells it, he saw orbital data centers coming. The Kenyan American engineer previously worked in Google’s cloud computing business before a brief stint at SpaceX’s Starlink communications network in 2024. His experiences convinced him that there was untapped potential for computers in space. “When I was at SpaceX, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no. When I was at Google, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no,” he tells TechCrunch. So he left SpaceX and co-founded Satlyt , a new company with headquarters in Sunnyvale, California, and Nairobi, to build software for satellites that he hopes will let many satellites share the work of large computing jobs in space. The company has raised an $8 million seed round, Afullo exclusively told TechCrunch. The timing looks good for him. SpaceX has since gone all-in on orbital data centers, and Satlyt’s software is set to launch Thursday on a SpaceX rocket alongside the first prototype for Google’s space data center effort, Project Suncatcher. Unlike SpaceX, Google, or startups like Starcloud and Cowboy Space Company, Satlyt isn’t planning to build its own spacecraft. Afullo’s team is building the software to operate AI models on satellites, comparing his approach to VMware and Snowflake — companies whose platforms let users run complex software without worrying about the underlying infrastructure. “The folks like SpaceX who are doing orbital data centers — if they are the iPhone, we’ll build Android as a horizontally integrated, open ecosystem,” he said. In other words, Satlyt wants to offer software that works across many companies’ satellites. Satlyt has already flown its software on two demonstration missions. The initial focus is finding operational efficiencies for spacecraft, which typically depend on flight controllers on the ground to solve any problems that arise. items.t: SpaceXSI bundles X Premium, Grok, and Cursor into one subscription
items.d: The new X Subscription combines X's paid features with AI tools like Grok and Cursor, offering plans ranging from $8 to $200 per month.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 6:50 AM PDT · October 13, 2026 Image Credits: X Corp. Sarah Perez SpaceXSI bundles X Premium, Grok, and Cursor into one subscription In a bid to attract more subscribers, the company now known as SpaceX Super Intelligence is bundling all its subscriptions, including X Premium, Grok, and Cursor, into one plan called simply “The X Subscription.” The idea is that the combined offering could potentially attract more subscribers than any single subscription, given the competitive paid AI subscription market, where SpaceXSI faces rivals like OpenAI, Anthropic, and others. With The X Subscription, users can gain access to Grok for AI-powered chat, with support for voice, images, video, and the API. Grok’s agentic AI Bot is also available, as is Cursor for AI coding and the paid features that come with an X Premium subscription, like the blue verified checkmark, creator tools, and fewer ads. There are five plans available on the new subscription: free, Plus ($8/month), Premium ($30/month), Super ($100/month), and Ultra ($200/month), with AI usage caps increasing as you move up through the tiers. The free plan will only offer limited chat and agent usage, and Premium or higher is required to access the latest Grok models. There’s another draw for existing X Premium+ subscribers: The comparable plan on the new X subscription costs the same or less, the company noted. Existing users can either switch from their subscription settings on X to upgrade to the new bundle, or maintain their current plan. The option to upgrade will roll out gradually, so interested customers will need to keep an eye on their billing settings for the offer to upgrade. SK하이닉스가 2013년 12월 세계 최초로 HBM을 상용화하는 과정에도 참여했다. 시상식은 오는 15일 대전 롯데시티호텔에서 열린다. 정지은 기자 jeong@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 정지은 기자 한국경제신문 산업부에서 전자업계를 담당하고 있습니다. 제보 메일 환영합니다. Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging
items.d: Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to become a major mobile carrier sent shares of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile plunging and wiped out over $50 billion before lunch.
items.fullText: Corporations Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging The company announced plans to “become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.” in part by buying spectrum and deploying satellites for its Starlink service. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Starlink's mobile internet business is the single biggest money maker for Elon Musk's flagship company, SpaceX. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 9, 2026, 1:55 PM EDT / Updated Oct. 9, 2026, 4:26 PM EDT By Steve Kopack Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to “become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.” sent shares of the nation’s big three wireless carriers sliding by double digits Friday, wiping out more than $50 billion in market value before lunch. “Once we receive final FCC approval, Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere,” the company said late Thursday. It also announced that the Federal Communications Commission had approved the launch of 15,000 new satellites, also under Starlink Mobile, which is a subsidiary of SpaceX. Shares of AT&T fell 9.8%, Verizon dropped 8.7%, while T-Mobile US plunged 13.3%. For Verizon, today’s performance was its worst-one day drop since 2002. It was T-Mobile’s worst day since 2011. Shares of Charter and of Comcast, the parent company of NBC News, also fell Friday. Both companies sell wireless services under their own brands using Verizon’s infrastructure. Musk’s empire expands The announcement from SpaceX marked Musk’s latest step to expand his global tech empire. The world’s richest man and its first-ever trillionaire , Musk’s net worth as of Thursday was about $990 billion. items.t: In new Elon Musk documentary, his lieutenants are the most damning voices
items.d: ‘Musk,’ the new film from Alex Gibney, features interviews with more than the usual critics of the Tesla and SpaceX CEO.
items.fullText: ANALYSIS Elon Musk Elon Musk In new Elon Musk documentary, his lieutenants are the most damning voices “Musk,” the new film from Alex Gibney, features interviews with more than the usual critics of the Tesla and SpaceX CEO. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 SpaceX CEO Elon Musk in Washington on Sept. 29. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 9, 2026, 5:00 AM EDT By David Ingram SAN RAFAEL, Calif. — It’s easy to find people with bad things to say about tech magnate Elon Musk, and plenty of those people show up in “Musk,” a new documentary about his rise to political and corporate power. What’s more surprising in the film are the unflattering statements by some of his own employees, including ones who still work for him. Some of the harshest scenes in the film, which opens Friday in Los Angeles and New York, are ones in which Musk’s lieutenants were recorded on video or in audio as they wielded power on his behalf or discussed what they had already done for him. Warning: This article includes spoilers for the documentary “Musk.” There are clips of Ashok Elluswamy, a high-ranking Tesla engineer, acknowledging in a videotaped deposition that an infamous hype video he helped put together in 2016 about the company’s self-driving capabilities was not an accurate representation of Tesla’s technology at the time. There are also audio snippets from Jared Birchall, who handles Musk’s personal matters. He is heard on a recording of a phone call with online influencer Ashley St. Clair, shortly after she had given birth to a child she and Musk conceived, in which he plays hardball on child support arrangements. Both incidents were documented in the media: Reuters reported in 2023 on the transcript of Elluswamy’s deposition , and The Wall Street Journal reported last year on Birchall’s phone call with St. Clair.
